answer: An FRI-based commitment encodes data as evaluations of a low-degree polynomial and proves proximity to that code by repeatedly folding the evaluations, so a verifier samples a few positions instead of reading everything. A mirror copy of a fake polynomial still fails the folding test, the tide of invented evaluations cannot stay low-degree under random folds, and a violet mark left by one bad coordinate spreads through the folding until a sampled check catches it.
